Title: Dedicated unattended checkout did not synchronize origin/main before building
Reproduction Steps: Leave the dedicated refresh clone at one clean main commit, advance private origin/main with an ordinary code/docs commit, then run the pre-fix real refresher. Inspect the new data commit parent, push result, and next scheduled attempt.
Expected Result: Before each real build, the dedicated clone fetches origin/main and proceeds only from equal history or a clean fast-forward; fetched orchestration code owns the transaction. Fetch/race/divergence/rewind fails closed, while one exactly verified unpushed data commit has a durable pinned retry path.
Actual Result: The refresher captured local HEAD without fetching. After any normal repository push, it would build and commit on the stale tip, fail its non-force push, then remain locally ahead/diverged on every weekly run. With no installed health timer, autonomous updates could stop until manual repair.
Evidence: The integration audit traced the installed topology before activation. Disposable Git fixtures reproduce remote-ahead, divergence, rewind, dirty-after-fetch, arbitrary local-ahead, and repeated push-retry states. The final suite passes 27/27 and proves the remote version of auto_refresh.py actually reexecutes after fast-forward.
Root Cause Hypothesis: The original transaction correctly protected its own candidate and push SHA but treated synchronization of its dedicated clone as an external host responsibility, leaving no code-level freshness boundary for the orchestrator itself.
Fix Plan: Add a real-run-only origin/main fetch boundary under the process lock; require clean main and tracking continuity; fast-forward-only then reexec fetched code with the inherited lock; reject all ambiguous histories; persist exact mode-0600 pending-push proof for one allowlisted local commit and retry it before another build. Keep dry-run ref-free.

Verification Evidence: PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp/volta-pycache python3 tests/test_auto_refresh.py -v -> 27/27 OK in an independent rerun; py_compile and git diff --check pass. The audit independently reran 27/27 and accepted the sync design subject to final host activation.

Fix Plan: Extract each method's body into _route_get/_route_head unchanged; wrap do_GET/do_HEAD with try/except BrokenPipeError (return) / except Exception (log the full traceback server-side via self.log_message, then send_json(500, {"error": "internal_error", ...}) for GET or a bare send_error(500) for HEAD; an inner try/except covers the headers-already-sent case).

Title: Seven module-level caches had unlocked check-then-act mutation from concurrent request threads; a torn read could serve one filter-set's cached payload under another's key
Reproduction Steps: Patch fetch_mapareve/fetch_gaia_live/fetch_fenie_live with tiny sleeps; run 16 threads x 30 iterations calling server.live_response with two alternating max_price filter sets (two distinct cache_keys) against the shared server.CACHE, under an aggressive sys.setswitchinterval(1e-6) to widen the race window; separately, hammer server.geocode_search from 8 threads with unique queries past the 500-entry GEOCODE_CACHE eviction threshold.
Expected Result: No exceptions from any thread; every returned payload's station set matches the max_price it was requested with (no cross-key bleed); the eviction loop tolerates concurrent inserts.
Actual Result: Reproduced concretely: AssertionError: cross-key bleed: requested max_price=0.24 but got station 'station-0.21' -- a torn read across CACHE's cache_fresh decide-then-deepcopy(CACHE["payload"]) let one thread observe another thread's just-written key/payload combination. (The eviction loops' RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration, the other symptom named in the originating plan, did NOT reproduce on this CPython 3.9.6 build even under an isolated adversarial probe: list(D.keys())[:N] snapshots into a plain list before the pop loop runs, and that list() conversion is GIL-atomic in this build -- confirmed by contrasting it against a direct for k in d.keys(): loop, which reproduced the RuntimeError immediately in the same probe. The underlying check-then-act is still unsynchronized and GIL-implementation-dependent -- it would not hold under free-threaded/no-GIL Python 3.13t or PyPy -- so the fix removes that dependency regardless of which exact exception type is reachable on a given build.)
Evidence: tests/test_request_resilience.py::ConcurrentLiveCacheStressTests pre-fix run captured the cross-key-bleed AssertionError above under sys.setswitchinterval(1e-6); reproduced in roughly 1 of 5-13 runs across default and aggressive scheduling, confirming the race is real but load/timing-dependent, not deterministic on every run.
Root Cause Hypothesis: CACHE, GAIA_CACHE, FENIE_CACHE, ELECTROMAPS_CACHE, GEOCODE_CACHE, OVERVIEW_BYTES_CACHE and STATIC_GZ_CACHE are module-level dicts mutated by concurrent ThreadingHTTPServer request threads (plus an 8-worker ThreadPoolExecutor fan-out within a single request) with zero synchronization.
Fix Plan: Add a _CACHE_LOCKS dict (one threading.Lock per cache: live/gaia/fenie/electromaps/geocode/overview/static_gz -- the exact convention plans 005 and 007 will reuse for their own shared state). Wrap ONLY each cache's read-decide/copy and write/evict sites in with _CACHE_LOCKS[name]:; the network fetch (or, for overview/static_gz, the CPU-only serialize/compress step) always stays OUTSIDE the lock. The benign "two threads both miss and both fetch" race is accepted and documented, not serialized.

Title: Unguarded ZoneInfo("Europe/Madrid") at module import could crash the server boot on a tzdata-less base image
Reproduction Steps: Call server._load_madrid_tz() (previously: the bare module-level `ZoneInfo("Europe/Madrid") if ZoneInfo else timezone.utc` expression) with server.ZoneInfo patched to raise (simulating zoneinfo being importable but the OS tz database missing, e.g. python:3.12-slim with no tzdata package installed -- ZoneInfo(...) raises zoneinfo.ZoneInfoNotFoundError in that case).
Expected Result: MADRID_TZ resolves to timezone.utc instead of propagating the exception, so the module (and therefore the whole server) still imports successfully.
Actual Result: Before the fix, the ZoneInfo("Europe/Madrid") call at module scope had no try/except around the lookup itself (only the earlier `from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo` import was guarded); a missing tz database would raise uncaught at import time, which `import server` (and therefore server startup) cannot recover from -- a genuine crash-loop on any base image without tzdata installed, not merely a degraded feature.
Evidence: tests/test_public_hardening.py::MadridTimezoneGuardTests -- test_falls_back_to_utc_when_zoneinfo_raises and test_falls_back_to_utc_when_zoneinfo_is_none patch server.ZoneInfo to raise/None and assert server._load_madrid_tz() returns timezone.utc; a real docker build of the (now tzdata-installing) image also confirms MADRID_TZ resolves to the real Europe/Madrid zone via `docker exec ... python -c "import server; print(server.MADRID_TZ)"`.
Root Cause Hypothesis: The Dockerfile's python:3.12-slim base was assumed to carry a full tz database; slim/minimal Debian images are not guaranteed to (and some slim variants ship without tzdata), and the code had no defensive fallback for the lookup itself failing, only for the zoneinfo module being absent (Python <3.9).
Fix Plan: Extract a _load_madrid_tz() helper: returns timezone.utc if ZoneInfo is falsy (unimportable), else try ZoneInfo("Europe/Madrid") and fall back to timezone.utc on ANY exception (not just import failure). MADRID_TZ = _load_madrid_tz(). Belt-and-suspenders: Dockerfile stage 2 also now installs tzdata explicitly (apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends tzdata) so production actually gets correct Madrid-local pricing-window boundaries -- the guard alone would silently run on UTC and shift overnight-window boundaries 1-2h, which is not acceptable for production, only as an outage-preventing safety net.
Fix Commit / Files Changed: server.py; Dockerfile; tests/test_public_hardening.py; qa/defects.csv; qa/test-cases.csv; qa/features.csv; qa/coverage-summary.md; qa/run-log.md
Verification Evidence: tests/test_public_hardening.py -v: 20/20 pass, including both MadridTimezoneGuardTests fallback cases; `python3 -c "import server; print(server.MADRID_TZ)"` -> Europe/Madrid on this host (tzdata present); real `docker build` of the updated Dockerfile succeeded, `docker exec <container> python -c "import server; print(server.MADRID_TZ)"` -> Europe/Madrid inside the container; full backend `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` -> 275/275 OK; ./scripts/verify.sh green.
Notes: The current python:3.12-slim (trixie) build already happened to carry tzdata ('tzdata is already the newest version' during the docker build), so this exact crash was not reproducible against today's upstream image -- but the unguarded call was still a latent defect against the Dockerfile's own stated base (any tzdata-less slim/minimal image), and the guard plus explicit install closes both the immediate crash risk and the correctness risk (UTC-shifted pricing windows) at once.

Title: Dockerfile silently fell back from `npm ci` to `npm install` on any failure, bypassing the lockfile's exact-version guarantee
Reproduction Steps: Inspect Dockerfile stage 1 (web): `RUN npm ci 2>/dev/null || npm install`. Any npm ci failure -- corrupted/out-of-sync package-lock.json, a registry hiccup, a peer-dependency conflict, anything -- silently falls through to `npm install`, which resolves and may rewrite the lockfile with different (potentially newer/untested) transitive versions instead of failing the build.
Expected Result: A lockfile/registry problem fails the Docker build loudly, the same way a local `npm ci` would, so drift is caught at build time instead of silently shipping unverified dependency versions.
Actual Result: The `2>/dev/null || npm install` fallback swallowed npm ci's stderr and exit code entirely and masked ANY cause of failure -- a genuinely corrupted lockfile looked identical in the build log to a normal first-time install.
Evidence: Dockerfile:6 (pre-fix) read `RUN npm ci 2>/dev/null || npm install`, verified on disk before this fix; a real `docker build` after the fix (bare `RUN npm ci`) completed successfully against the current, valid frontend/package-lock.json, confirming the strict path still works for the normal case.
Root Cause Hypothesis: The fallback was presumably added at some point to unblock a build when the lockfile and package.json had drifted locally, then never removed -- a convenience during development that becomes a supply-chain/reproducibility risk in a production image build.
Fix Plan: Replace with a bare `RUN npm ci`, matching the project's own stated intent (frontend/package-lock.json is the source of truth) and letting a real lockfile problem fail the build instead of silently reinstalling.
Fix Commit / Files Changed: Dockerfile; qa/defects.csv; qa/test-cases.csv; qa/features.csv; qa/coverage-summary.md; qa/run-log.md
Verification Evidence: Real `docker build -t volta-hardening-test .` (colima-backed Docker, arm64) completed successfully end-to-end with the bare `RUN npm ci` (stage 1 `web`), through `RUN npm run build`, into the stage-2 Python runtime, `RUN python -c "import server"`, and image tag; `docker run` of the built image booted and `/api/health` returned 200 with `{"ok":true,...}`.
Notes: Confirmed via `grep -n "npm ci" Dockerfile` that no `|| npm install` fallback remains.

Title: Client-visible warnings and error lists carried raw upstream exception text instead of the exception class name only
Reproduction Steps: Patch server.fetch_mapareve to raise RuntimeError("secret-internal-detail") and call server.live_response({"max_price": ["0.25"], "force": ["false"]}) with an empty CACHE (no stale fallback available). Also: server.fetch_fenie_live, the fetch_electromaps_live call site in live_response, fetch_mapareve's own per-page error accumulation (payload["errors"]), and fetch_gaia_live's per-seed error accumulation all interpolated f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}" (or equivalent) directly into structures that reach the client.
Expected Result: Client-visible text (payload["warning"], payload["gaia"/"fenie"/"electromaps"]["errors"/"error"], and CACHE["error"] as exposed via /api/health) contains the exception CLASS name only (e.g. RuntimeError); the exception MESSAGE -- which can carry upstream-internal detail such as internal URLs, library-internal strings, or connection detail -- never reaches the client. Full detail is still available server-side for debugging.
Actual Result: Before the fix, `err = f"{type(mapareve_error).__name__}: {mapareve_error}"` (and the four other sites above) put the full exception message straight into client-visible JSON with no server-side-only logging of the detail at all -- an anonymous public caller could see, and possibly learn from, internal exception text on every upstream hiccup.
Evidence: tests/test_public_hardening.py::WarningSanitizationTests::test_mapareve_failure_warning_hides_exception_message failed pre-fix (assertNotIn("secret-internal-detail", ...) found the string present in the response) and passes post-fix; a live run against a real server showed the sanitized site logging the full detail server-side (`MapaREVE live refresh failed: RuntimeError: secret-internal-detail`) while the client response body contained only `RuntimeError`.
Root Cause Hypothesis: The fail-closed warning voice ("nothing is presented as live") was designed around honesty about live-data status, not around what a raw exception's __str__ might leak; error interpolation sites were added ad hoc across five call sites (mapareve_error in live_response, fetch_mapareve's per-page loop, fetch_fenie_live, the fetch_electromaps_live call site, and fetch_gaia_live's per-seed loop) with no shared sanitization convention.
Fix Plan: At each of the five sites: keep only `type(exc).__name__` in the client-visible string/list; add a new server-side-only `_log_upstream_error(context, exc)` helper (ISO-8601 UTC timestamped print, matching the newly-sanitized log_message format) that logs the full `type(exc).__name__: {exc}` string once, right where the exception is caught. Checked tests/test_live_coverage.py's warning-text assertions first, per plan: all of them assert fixed-prefix substrings that appear BEFORE the interpolated exception detail (e.g. "Live source unavailable", "Live refresh failed; serving stale cache") -- none pinned the raw injected message text ("blocked ip" / "upstream down"), so zero assertions needed updating.
Fix Commit / Files Changed: server.py; tests/test_public_hardening.py; qa/defects.csv; qa/test-cases.csv; qa/features.csv; qa/coverage-summary.md; qa/run-log.md
Verification Evidence: tests/test_public_hardening.py -v: 20/20 pass; tests/test_live_coverage.py -v: 10/10 pass UNCHANGED (confirms no assertion pinned the raw message); full backend `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` -> 275/275 OK; ./scripts/verify.sh green; live curl smoke against a running server showed no leaked detail in any /api/chargers or /api/health response body.
Notes: CACHE["error"] is also exposed via GET /api/health (`{k: v for k, v in CACHE.items() if k != "payload"}`); sanitizing the shared `err` variable in live_response's mapareve-failure branch closes both that site and the payload["warning"] site with one fix.

Title: Live and overview request paths repeated expensive work on every request even on a cache hit: intel-lead enrichment reran per call, O(n*m) merge/dedup scans, and both the live and overview byte caches evicted on any filter/bbox change
Reproduction Steps: Run PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp/volta-pycache python3 scripts/perf_probe.py (pre-fix, commit 56a4010's parent 0c93482): load_all_leads(SPAIN_BBOX) re-normalizes+re-enriches all ~958 in-view intel/seed records on every call regardless of prior calls (cold 228.6ms, warm 210.0ms -- zero reuse); remove_duplicate_leads(958 leads x 300 stations) does a full O(n*m) likely_same_station scan per lead pair, 740.5ms; overview_response(compact=true) 236.1ms (dominated by the same unmemoized enrichment). Separately: live_response's raw MapaREVE cache_fresh branch still re-ran merges/dedup/the full per-station enrich_station loop on every hit (no assembled-payload reuse existed); OVERVIEW_BYTES_CACHE was a single "entry" slot keyed by the full (mtime,mtime,max_price,fast_only,compact) tuple, so alternating between two filter states (A,B,A,B) never hit cache; the SPA's instant first-paint layer always calls overview=true WITH a bbox (frontend/src/lib/api.ts chargersUrl), which bypassed the bytes cache entirely (Handler._route_get only served the no-bbox case).
Expected Result: Repeated requests for already-known data reuse prior work: a warm intel-lead load is a bbox-filter+deepcopy of a memoized enriched list, not a re-normalize; the pairwise merge/dedup helpers use a spatial+identity index instead of a full O(n*m) scan; a live cache hit whose sub-sources also served a fresh hit reuses the assembled (merged+enriched) payload instead of rebuilding it; the overview byte cache holds several concurrent filter/bbox combinations instead of one.
Actual Result: Every one of the four sub-issues reproduced with real measured evidence (see scripts/perf_probe.py output below and qa/run-log.md's Iteration 174 before/after table): warm load_all_leads(SPAIN_BBOX) 210.0ms, remove_duplicate_leads(958x300) 740.5ms, merge_gaia_stations(300x150) 25.3ms, overview_response(compact=true) 236.1ms -- all with zero cross-call reuse; a live_response cache_fresh hit paid the full enrich_station cost per station on every request; OVERVIEW_BYTES_CACHE's single slot made two alternating filter states thrash (test_alternating_filter_toggle_both_serve_from_cache_on_repeat characterizes this: pre-fix, both repeat calls would have been misses); a bbox-carrying overview=true request (the SPA's own default first-paint pattern) never touched the bytes cache at all.
Evidence: scripts/perf_probe.py (created this iteration) BEFORE (pre-step-2, commit 56a4010^): load_all_leads warm 210.0ms, remove_duplicate_leads(958x300) 740.5ms, merge_gaia_stations(300x150) 25.3ms, overview_response(compact=true) 236.1ms. AFTER (post-step-5, this defect's fix): load_all_leads warm 80.6ms (2.6x), remove_duplicate_leads(958x300) 8.1ms (91x), merge_gaia_stations(300x150) 2.6ms (10x), overview_response(compact=true) 91.5ms (2.6x -- the residual cost is now dominated by leads NOT in the memoized-and-shared enriched pool's fast path, i.e. per-request corroboration+sort over ~957 rows). Live-server smoke (real ThreadingHTTPServer on 127.0.0.1:8791, PORT env, current data/free_intelligence.json): overview_response_bytes for a Valencia bbox, cache MISS (compute+json.dumps+gzip) 32.7ms vs cache HIT 0.1ms (327x). tests/test_perf_invariants.py::AssembledPayloadReuseTests::test_second_call_within_ttl_reuses_assembled_payload_without_reenrichment proves a mock-wrapped server.enrich_station is called 0 times on a second, cache-eligible live_response call within TTL (unittest.mock wraps-counter, not an inferred timing signal). Full table with real command output for both the BEFORE and AFTER runs is in qa/run-log.md's Iteration 174 entry.
Root Cause Hypothesis: The enrichment pipeline (_normalize_lead/enrich_station), the O(n*m) source-merge/dedup helpers, and the two byte-serialization caches were each built and extended incrementally (plans 003/004/005/008/009) to fix correctness/security issues at national scale, without anyone re-examining whether the per-request cost of the now-much-larger national intel DB (~955 records, vs. the original Valencia-only scope) was being amortized across requests. Each individual addition was locally reasonable; the aggregate effect was that a cache "hit" (by name) still did nearly all the same CPU work as a miss.
Fix Plan: Five-step perf rewrite (plans/007), each step verified independently against the plans/006 characterization-test safety net before landing: (1) scripts/perf_probe.py + tests/test_perf_invariants.py baseline/equality harness, landed first so every later step has a before/after and a golden-equality proof. (2) _INTEL_ENRICHED: memoize the fully normalized+enriched intel-DB+seed-lead universe (no bbox filter) keyed by (db mtime, seeds mtime), guarded by a new _CACHE_LOCKS["intel"]; load_intelligence/load_all_leads/load_seed_leads now bbox-filter (via a prebuilt coord array) and deepcopy only the in-view subset instead of re-normalizing the whole DB. (3) _station_match_index/_match_candidates: a ~0.002deg grid + url + id index shared by merge_gaia_stations/remove_duplicate_leads/merge_fenie_stations, pruning their O(n*m) scans to a small ascending-index candidate set; the matchers themselves are unchanged. (4) live_response's tail split into Phase A (merge/dedup/enrich, cacheable) and Phase B (per-request distance/eta/sort, always runs); the fully-fresh Phase A output is cached in CACHE["assembled"] and reused on a later cache_fresh hit only when gaia/fenie also report a fresh non-stale hit and no electromaps live work happened at write time (electromaps has no per-call cache.hit flag reliable enough to re-verify freshness for a different request, so its involvement permanently excludes an entry from reuse rather than risk serving stale data as fresh). (5) OVERVIEW_BYTES_CACHE keyed by the full tuple (FIFO-capped at 8) instead of one slot; a second, separately-capped (16) OVERVIEW_BBOX_BYTES_CACHE serves the SPA's bbox-carrying overview=true requests, which previously bypassed caching entirely.

Title: Assembled live-payload cache reuse (plans/007 step 4) could serve a write-time-stale gaia/fenie row as fresh with no stale warning
Reproduction Steps: On-demand adviser review of plans/007 (not yet pushed) found: server.py's live_response wrote CACHE["assembled"] gated ONLY on mapareve_fresh_fetch (~3975-3985 pre-fix), never checking whether gaia/fenie were themselves serving a stale fallback when the assembled entry was built; the reuse-read gate (~3776-3782 pre-fix) checked only THIS request's gaia/fenie hit/!stale, never that the reader's gaia/fenie data equals what was merged at write time. Adviser repro scripts (scratchpad, not committed): repro_reuse.py Repro A and repro_a2.py -- call1: MapaREVE fresh fetch + gaia serving a STALE fallback (cache.stale=True) whose payload contains an AVAILABLE gaia station 'gaia-1'; call2 (within TTL): MapaREVE cache_fresh hit, gaia genuinely refetched and now empty (cache.stale=False, station gone from the real feed). Real command output against pre-fix code (git stash of this iteration's own server.py changes, via repro_a2.py): "call1 warning: 'Gaia public-page refresh is slow...'" / "call2 warning: 'Low live coverage: 1/3 live stations under cap...'" / "call2 gaia-1 present: True" -- gaia-1 served on call2 with a FRESH gaia meta.cache and no gaia-stale text in the warning.
Expected Result: A row that only exists in the response because gaia/fenie were serving a stale fallback at write time must never be reusable by a later request just because gaia/fenie look fresh at read time; reuse must require the read's gaia/fenie data to be the SAME population that was merged at write time.
Actual Result: call2 incorrectly reused call1's merged snapshot and served the write-time-stale gaia-1 row as status=AVAILABLE, decision.level=go, verification.live_verified=True, route_ready_now=True, with no stale warning at all -- indistinguishable from a genuinely live, currently-available station.
Evidence: New rail test tests/test_perf_invariants.py::AssembledWriteRefusesStaleSubSourceTests::test_write_time_stale_gaia_row_is_never_served_as_fresh_on_a_later_reuse run against pre-fix server.py (git stash): FAIL -- "AssertionError: {... id: gaia-1 ...} is not None : assembled must NOT be written when gaia was stale at write time" (the dumped call1 assembled entry shows gaia-1 with decision.level=go and verification.live_verified=True, confirming the severity). Post-fix: same test passes; full tests/test_perf_invariants.py 18/18 (3 consecutive runs); full backend python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -> Ran 330 tests ... OK (expected failures=6) (was 325).
Root Cause Hypothesis: plans/007 step 4 (this iteration's own uncommitted work) added the assembled-payload cache as a request-path performance optimization; the write gate was written to prevent reuse from a MapaREVE stale/fallback branch (the risk the plan's STOP conditions explicitly called out) but never considered that gaia/fenie -- fetched and merged independently, each with their OWN cache/TTL/stale-fallback semantics -- could ALSO be stale at the exact moment the assembled snapshot was built, and the reuse gate's freshness check was written against "is it fresh NOW" (this request's own gaia/fenie payload) rather than "is it the SAME data that was actually merged".
Fix Plan: (1) fetch_gaia_live/fetch_fenie_live now stamp a stable populated_at epoch (the underlying cache slot's last-populated time, distinct from age_seconds which drifts with "now") into every cache-info dict they return. (2) The assembled WRITE now additionally requires gaia_cache_info/fenie_cache_info to be non-stale THIS request before writing at all; when mapareve_fresh_fetch is true but gaia/fenie was stale, no new assembled entry is written AND any OLD assembled entry under the same cache_key is explicitly cleared (it now reflects a MapaREVE fetch that CACHE["payload"] has already moved past). (3) The REUSE read gate additionally requires the read's gaia/fenie populated_at to exactly equal what was stored at write time (data identity), not merely "hit and not stale right now".

Title: Assembled live-payload cache reuse (plans/007 step 4) could silently drop in-view live stations when a read bbox shared a snapped tile with a narrower write bbox

Title: freshness_minutes/recommendation_score returned by load_intelligence/load_all_leads were frozen at intel-DB memo-pool build time, lagging real elapsed time by up to a DB-refresh interval
Reproduction Steps: plans/007 step 2's _INTEL_ENRICHED memo enriches every intel/seed record ONCE per (db mtime, seeds mtime) key; enrich_station stamps freshness_minutes=age_minutes(last_seen) (and recommendation_score, which reads freshness_minutes) at that single build moment. load_intelligence/load_all_leads (pre-fix) returned bbox-filtered deepcopies of the cached, already-enriched records with NO further processing, so every request served the SAME freshness_minutes/recommendation_score value for as long as the memo pool stayed valid -- up to a full weekly DB-refresh interval (scripts/refresh_intelligence.sh). frontend/src/lib/format.ts's ageText helper prefers the API's freshness_minutes field over recomputing from last_seen client-side, so this reached the rendered lead evidence-age text on both /api/chargers leads and /api/intel.
Expected Result: A lead's displayed evidence age (and the score derived from it) should reflect real elapsed time since last_seen on every request, not just at the moment the enrichment memo happened to last rebuild.
Actual Result: Two load_intelligence(None) calls straddling a change to a record's last_seen (simulated without touching the DB file, which would legitimately rebuild the whole pool and mask the bug) returned the SAME frozen freshness_minutes both times, ignoring the updated last_seen entirely.
Evidence: New rail test tests/test_perf_invariants.py::TimeDerivedFieldsRecomputeOnReturnTests::test_freshness_minutes_reflects_a_moved_last_seen_across_two_memo_hit_calls run against pre-fix server.py (git stash): FAIL -- "AssertionError: unexpectedly None" (old_freshness, read immediately after setting last_seen to a 2020 timestamp, was still the ORIGINAL frozen value from whenever the memo pool last built -- for the specific first DB record this test happened to pick, that frozen value was itself None, starkly proving freshness_minutes was completely decoupled from the returned last_seen). Post-fix: the same test passes, asserting old_freshness reflects the 2020 timestamp (>1 year in minutes), new_freshness (after moving last_seen to now) is <5 minutes, the two differ, recommendation_score differs too (it depends on freshness_minutes), and load_all_leads (the other public accessor) recomputes identically.
Root Cause Hypothesis: plans/007 step 2 was designed to memoize the EXPENSIVE part of enrichment (the full enrich_station pipeline: verification/decision/pricing/parking/etc, ~190ms for the whole DB) -- freshness_minutes/recommendation_score were swept into that same memo as a side effect of being computed inside enrich_station, without separating "expensive, safe to memoize" fields from "cheap, must stay live" ones. tests/test_perf_invariants.py's own pre-existing LoadAllLeadsSelfEqualityTests explicitly strips these two fields before comparing (with a docstring calling out the tradeoff as "disclosed") -- the tradeoff was known and accepted for the equality-gate tests, but its product-facing consequence (stale evidence-age text on cards) was not separately evaluated against AGENTS.md's Trust UX expectations until this adviser review.
Fix Plan: A new _refresh_time_derived_fields(records) helper recomputes freshness_minutes=age_minutes(last_seen) and recommendation_score=recommendation_score(record) -- pure, O(n) arithmetic, freshness_minutes first since recommendation_score reads it -- on the already-deepcopied in-view subset load_intelligence/load_all_leads are about to return. It mutates only the caller's own fresh copies, never the memo pool itself, so the expensive enrich_station pass stays memoized exactly as before; only these two cheap, wall-clock-dependent fields are now live on every call.

Title: iOS ChargersResponse whole-array decode failure on a single coord-less lead blanks the entire station/lead list
Reproduction Steps: ios/Volta/Volta/Models.swift (pre-fix) declared struct ChargersResponse: Decodable { var stations: [Station]; var leads: [Station]; ... } with Station's id/name/lat/lon all non-optional. server.py's _normalize_lead/enrich_station (server.py ~3133-3164, ~975-994) never backfill lat/lon on a lead dict that never had those keys, so a manual/municipal lead recorded by name only (no coordinates) serializes to JSON with no lat/lon key at all. Confirmed the current DB has none (a scan of data/free_intelligence.json (954 records) and data/seed_leads.json (5 records) found 0 missing coords), matching plans/README.md's own 'Latent today (current DB has none)' note -- a real, verified, currently-dormant defect, not a live outage.
Expected Result: A single coord-less row in the stations/leads JSON arrays must never abort decoding the rest of the array -- Swift's JSONDecoder.decode([Station].self, ...) throws on the FIRST element that fails to decode (missing/null non-optional field), which would blank the ENTIRE list on the iOS client the moment one such row appears.
Actual Result: ios/Volta/Volta/VoltaAPI.swift's generic get<T: Decodable> calls Self.decoder.decode(T.self, from: data) where T = ChargersResponse and ChargersResponse.stations/.leads were plain [Station]; a coord-less element anywhere in either array throws DecodingError.keyNotFound/.valueNotFound for lat/lon, which propagates out of the WHOLE array decode and out of ChargersResponse.init(from:), so VoltaAPI.overview()/.live() throw and AppState receives no stations/leads at all -- not just the one bad row, everything.
Evidence: New guard tests/test_ios_design_contract.py::IOSDesignContractTests::test_chargers_response_drops_coordless_rows_instead_of_crashing_the_whole_list, run against pre-fix Models.swift via `git stash push -- ios/Volta/Volta/Models.swift && python3 tests/test_ios_design_contract.py -v`: FAIL -- "AssertionError: '@propertyWrapper' not found in ..." (confirms the pre-fix file had no lenient-decode mechanism at all). `git stash pop` restored the fix and the same run passed 6/6.
Root Cause Hypothesis: Models.swift's own header comment already documented the intended contract ('everything but identity/coords is optional') as a deliberate per-FIELD design choice mirroring the web client's optional confidence/source fields, but nobody had separately reasoned about ARRAY-level partial-decode tolerance -- Swift's synthesized Decodable conformance for a plain [Station] has no such tolerance built in (unlike, say, a hand-rolled JS .map()/.filter() pipeline on the web client, which silently skips a malformed row by construction). server.py's lead pipeline was written to allow name-only leads (a legitimate, honest 'we know this exists but have no coordinate evidence yet' state) without anyone separately auditing what every CONSUMER of /api/chargers does with such a row.
Fix Plan: Add a small, reusable @propertyWrapper struct LossyArray<Element: Decodable>: Decodable (Models.swift) that decodes a JSON array element-by-element via an inner never-throwing wrapper (Element_, using try? so the unkeyed container's cursor always advances -- no risk of stalling on a malformed element), dropping any element that fails to decode. Apply it to ChargersResponse.stations/.leads only (@LossyArray var stations: [Station] / @LossyArray var leads: [Station]); leave Station.id/.lat/.lon non-optional and every other .lat/.lon/.coordinate call site across RootView/StationViews/SheetView/AppState untouched, since the property wrapper is transparent to callers (resp.stations still reads as plain [Station]). Title: Map camera re-centers/re-zooms on every 60s live poll while a station is selected, overriding the driver's manual pan/zoom
Reproduction Steps: frontend/src/components/MapView.tsx (pre-fix, ~lines 709-734): a single useEffect handled BOTH the station-selected highlight filter AND map.flyTo(...), with dependency array [selectedId, stations]. stations is a fresh array reference on every ~60s live-poll refresh (TanStack Query refetch, per AGENTS.md section 7's documented ~60s client refresh) even when every station's VALUES are unchanged -- React's effect-dependency comparison is reference equality, so a new stations array reference alone re-fires the effect and re-invokes map.flyTo(...) for the currently selected station on every poll, even though the user never touched the selection and may have since manually panned/zoomed elsewhere.
Expected Result: The camera should fly to a station ONLY when the SELECTION itself changes (a genuine user action: tapping a card/pin) -- a background data refresh must never move the camera out from under the driver's own pan/zoom.
Actual Result: Every ~60s poll (even one that changes nothing about the selected station) called map.flyTo({ center: [st.lon, st.lat], zoom: Math.max(map.getZoom(), 14), speed: 0.8, ... }) again, snapping the camera back to the selected station and re-zooming to at least 14, discarding any manual pan/zoom the driver had done in the meantime.
Evidence: Code inspection of the pre-fix effect (git show HEAD:frontend/src/components/MapView.tsx lines ~709-734: single effect, deps [selectedId, stations]; stations was never referenced inside the effect body except via the ALREADY-current stationsByIdRef.current ref, i.e. stations was dead weight in the deps array with the side effect of also re-arming flyTo on every reference change) plus TanStack Query's documented ~60s refetch behavior confirm the mechanism. Found and verified by static/structural analysis plus the standard build/lint/test gates -- no dedicated runtime browser assertion of live camera motion was performed, since MapLibre GL needs WebGL (impractical under jsdom/Vitest), matching this dispatch's own documented fallback for this specific case.
Root Cause Hypothesis: The original effect's comment ('Selection change -> highlight + fly') and its [selectedId, stations] deps array were written together as ONE unit handling two genuinely different concerns: (1) re-asserting the highlight filter against whatever paintStations most recently painted (which DOES legitimately want to re-run whenever stations changes) and (2) moving the camera (which should ONLY happen on a real selection change). Because stationsByIdRef.current (a ref, always current) was already being used to look up the flyTo target rather than a stations closure variable, the stations dependency was never actually NEEDED for the flyTo half of the effect -- but nobody had split the two concerns into separate effects, so the flyTo half inherited a dependency it never used and didn't need.
Fix Plan: Split the single effect into two. Effect 1 (unchanged deps [selectedId, stations]) keeps ONLY the map.setFilter('station-selected', ...) call. Effect 2 (NEW, deps [selectedId] only) contains ONLY the map.flyTo(...) call, reading the target station via selectedId ? stationsByIdRef.current.get(selectedId) : undefined (the same ref-based lookup as before, now the SOLE reason that data access works without a stations dependency). Preserved the existing reduced-motion spread (...(prefersReducedMotion() ? { duration: 0 } : null)) and the documented duration:undefined NaN-camera-wedge warning comment verbatim, moved into the new effect since it specifically explains the flyTo call.

Title: iOS Station model had no chargeClaim/parkingClaim fields, so JSONDecoder silently dropped the backend's two distinct provenance claims on every station/lead row
Reproduction Steps: server.py's ensure_claim_contract() (server.py:750-795) ALWAYS attaches both charge_claim (charging-PRICE provenance: type/source/url/price_min/summary) and parking_claim (parking-COST provenance: kind/source/url/cost_hint/summary) to every enriched station/lead row -- AGENTS.md Prime Directive #1 requires these two provenance claims stay tracked SEPARATELY, and they may disagree (claim_conflict). The web decodes and renders both independently (frontend/src/types.ts:181-182 Claim fields on Station; frontend/src/components/SourceProvenance.tsx:52-74 two distinct "Charging claim"/"Parking claim" blocks, each with its own source link). ios/Volta/Volta/Models.swift's Station struct (pre-fix) had no chargeClaim/parkingClaim properties at all -- Swift's Decodable synthesis silently ignores JSON keys with no matching property, so both charge_claim and parking_claim were dropped on every decode. Only claimConflict.summary (the conflict TEXT) survived and rendered in StationDetailView (StationViews.swift, "Sources disagree" row) -- the app could tell a driver two sources disagreed but never showed WHAT either source actually claimed or WHERE each came from.
Expected Result: Every station/lead row's charge_claim and parking_claim JSON, when present (server.py attaches both universally via ensure_claim_contract), decodes into two independent Claim structs on Station, each retaining its own type/source/url/price/cost/summary, and StationDetailView renders them as two visually distinct "Trust & provenance" blocks -- never merged into one, matching the web's SourceProvenance.tsx.

A station/lead JSON payload carrying distinct charge_claim/parking_claim decoded to a Station with both fields simply absent from memory (no compile error, no runtime crash -- Decodable's default behavior for unmatched keys is silent, which is exactly the honesty risk: nothing signals the data was lost).
